findings: Active-layer pixel and Smart Filter masks appear as temporary channel rows even when RGB is the editing target; both can coexist.
Clicking a mask row selects its existing mask edit target without automatically isolating the display. Mask-eye changes retain the current editing target.
Hiding image components with the mask eye visible displays grayscale. Selecting RGB returns to image view and hides mask eyes.
A vector mask is shown in Paths; it is not an additional raster channel row in the tested document.
Backslash toggles a raster-mask overlay while retaining RGB editing. With both masks and RGB active, the observed shortcut chose the layer mask after prior Filter Mask editing.
Quick Mask and saved alpha coexist with the temporary mask rows. Exact row ordering/name changes across creation contexts require further qualification.
APIReview: Existing channel.view selects layerMask/smartFilterMask but rejects visible on them. Planned expansion must share native eye/view state and keep target selection distinct; no new published Adobe route inferred.
